name: Wang Po
bio: Wang Po (AD 648–676) is counted among the four eminent poets of the early T’ang dynasty. He died young, by drowning on a voyage.
The poems here are Herbert A. Giles’s versions in Chinese Poetry in English Verse (1898), given with the poet’s name as spelled in that book.

poems.title: Ichabod
poems.author: Wang Po
poems.text:
Near these islands a palace was built by a prince,
But its music and song have departed long since;
The hill-mists of morning sweep down on the halls,
At night the red curtains lie furled on the walls.
The clouds o'er the water their shadows still cast.
Things change like the stars: how few autumns have passed
And yet where is that prince? Where is he?
— No reply.
Save the plash of the stream rolling ceaselessly by.

poems.title: A King of Tang
poems.author: Wang Po
poems.text:
There looms a lordly pleasure-tower o’er yon dim shore,
Raised by some King of Tang.
Jade pendants at his girdle clashed, and golden bells
Around his chariot rang.

Strange guests through sounding halls at dawn go trailing by,
Grey mists and mocking winds;
And sullen brooding twilights break in rain on rain,
To lash the ragged blinds.

The slow, sun-dappled clouds lean down o’er waters blue,
Clear mirrored one by one;
Then drift as all the world shall drift. The very stars
Their timeless courses run.

How many autumn moons have steeped those palace walls!
And paled the shattered beams!
What is their royal builder now? A Lord of dust?
An Emperor of dreams?

poems.title: Farewell to Vice-Prefect Tu Setting Out for His Official Post in Shu
poems.author: Wang Po
poems.translator: trans. Witter Bynner and Kiang Kang-hu (1929)
poems.text:
By this wall that surrounds the three Ch'in districts,
Through a mist that makes five rivers one,
We bid each other a sad farewell,
We two officials going opposite ways. . . .
And yet, while China holds our friendship,
And heaven remains our neighbourhood,
Why should you linger at the fork of the road,
Wiping your eyes like a heart-broken child?

poems.title: 送杜少府之任蜀州 (Song du shao fu zhi ren shu zhou)
poems.author: Wang Po
poems.collection: 唐詩三百首 (Three Hundred Tang Poems)
poems.note: 五言律詩. Also titled 送杜少府之任蜀川.
poems.text:
城闕輔三秦，風煙望五津。
與君離別意，同是宦遊人。
海內存知己，天涯若比鄰。
無爲在歧路，兒女共沾巾。
